title: Calling the internet
simple: Before broadband, the computer phoned the internet. Its modem dialled a number, and when the internet company’s modem answered, the two whistled and screeched at each other until they agreed how to talk. Then your parcels went down the phone line as sounds, very slowly, and nobody else could use the phone.
technical: A V.34 modem call: DTMF dialling, the answer tone, V.8 negotiation and line probing, then up to 28.8 kbit/s each way, less on a noisy line. The exchange switches a 64 kbit/s circuit, one timeslot on its trunk, for the whole call. PPP runs over it to log you in and hand out an address.

describe.simple: A phone line runs from the computer to the telephone exchange and on to the internet company’s modems. A speech bubble says the sounds: beeps, a ring, a long whistle and a screech, then connected. Cards show the steps, a photo arriving line by line, and the phone being busy.
describe.technical: The call runs as copper to the exchange, then a 64 kbit/s circuit to the ISP's modem bank. Waves show DTMF, the answer tone, V.34 training, then slow data. Cards show the handshake steps, a 30 kB photo taking about 8 seconds, and the call holding timeslot 7 of a 32-slot trunk.

slowSub.simple: Today it’s there in a blink.

circuitSub: Held all call, even when quiet
